turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to give Owen a zero, and why he found out from his phone in the middle of a class. Nobody called me first.
Thanks for coming in. I owe you an apology: the zero went in before I called you.
Okay. That's procedure 4.2, and you broke it. Now tell me what you based the zero on.
I am withdrawing the zero today. Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch. Nothing goes on his record. I will email you that tonight.

I'm writing that down: withdrawn today, nothing on his record, email tonight. But if the zero's gone, Owen's essay stands as written, so why does he need a rewrite at all? A rewrite says you still have a concern, Hale, and you haven't shown me one.
Here it is in writing, signed.
I'll keep this, Hale. Signed is good, and nothing on his record is the part I care about most. It still doesn't answer my question: on what basis does Owen write anything again?
Thank you for your time, Ms. Kalinowski.
We're not finished, Hale. Either you tell me what the concern is, or the rewrite comes off that page and the essay's mark goes back in. I'm not leaving with half an answer.
Then I'm going to the principal's office now, with this page and your procedure 4.3. You'll hear from me tonight.
